items.title: Ten Ways a Degenerate Age Disturbs the Mind, and Why Rarity Itself Becomes a Reason to Vow

items.zh: 謂多愚癡、多無慚愧、多諸慳嫉、多諸憂苦、多諸麁重、多諸煩惱、多諸惡行、多諸放逸、多諸懈怠、多諸不信。
items.en: Much delusion, much shamelessness, much stinginess and envy, much grief and distress, much unwieldiness of body and mind, much affliction, much wrongdoing, much heedlessness, much laziness, much lack of faith.

items.zh: 見是事已，便作是念：大濁惡世，於今正起諸隨煩惱所惱亂時，能發下劣聲聞、獨覺菩提心者，尚難可得，況於無上正等菩提能發心者。我當應發大菩提心，令此惡世無量有情，隨學於我起菩提願。
items.en: Having seen this, one thinks: in this vast, degenerate world, now disturbed by these derivative afflictions, even those able to raise the lesser resolve of a hearer or solitary buddha are hard to find — how much more so anyone raising the resolve for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. I myself should raise the great resolve for awakening, so that the boundless beings of this degenerate world may follow my example and likewise raise the aspiration for awakening.

items.zh: 由見末劫難得發心增上力故，於大菩提深生信解，因斯發起大菩提心。是名第四初發心緣。云何四因？

items.title: Section: Four Causes Behind the Resolve — Lineage, a Genuine Teacher, Compassion, and Fearlessness Before Suffering

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩種姓具足，是名第一初發心因。又諸菩薩賴佛菩薩善友攝受，是名第二初發心因。又諸菩薩於諸眾生多起悲心，是名第三初發心因。又諸菩薩於極長時種種猛利無間無缺生死大苦難行苦行無有怯畏，是名第四初發心因。
items.en: Bodhisattvas possessing complete lineage — this is the first cause of the initial resolve. Bodhisattvas relying on being embraced by a genuine spiritual friend among the buddhas and bodhisattvas — this is the second cause. Bodhisattvas frequently giving rise to compassion for beings — this is the third cause. Bodhisattvas facing, over an extremely long time, fierce, unbroken, unremitting suffering in birth and death, and difficult practices, without any fear — this is the fourth cause.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩六處殊勝，從無始世展轉傳來，法爾所得，當知是名種姓具足。由四種相，當知菩薩善友具足。

謂諸菩薩所遇善友，性不愚鈍，聰明黠慧，不墮惡見，是名第一善友具足。又諸菩薩所遇善友，終不教人行於放逸，亦不授與諸放逸具，是名第二善友具足。又諸菩薩所遇善友，終不教人行於惡行，亦不授與諸惡行具。是名第三善友具足。又諸菩薩所遇善友，終不勸捨增上信、欲、受學、精進、方便功德，而復勸修下劣信、欲、受學、精進、方便功德。所謂終不勸捨大乘，勸修二乘；勸捨修慧，勸修思慧；勸捨思慧，勸修聞慧；勸捨聞慧，勸修福業；勸捨尸羅，勸修慧施。終不勸捨如是等類增上功德，而復勸修如是等類下劣功德。是名第四善友具足。
items.en: A bodhisattva's genuine spiritual friend is by nature neither dull nor slow, but intelligent and discerning, never falling into wrong views — this is the first mark of a genuine friend … never teaching another to be heedless … never teaching another to do wrong … and never urging one to abandon superior confidence, aspiration, training, diligence, or skilful means in favour of something inferior — this is the fourth mark.

items.zh: 由四因緣，當知菩薩於諸眾生多起悲心。
謂諸菩薩雖有十方無量無邊無苦世界，而生有苦諸世界中。於中恒有眾苦可得，非無眾苦。或時見他隨遭一苦觸對逼切，或時見自隨遭一苦觸對逼切，或見自他隨遭一苦觸對逼切，或見二種俱遭長時種種猛利無間大苦觸對逼切。然此菩薩依自種姓，性自仁賢。依四境處，雖不串習，而能發起下中上悲，無有斷絕。由四因緣，當知菩薩於諸眾生先起悲心，於極長時種種猛利無間無缺生死大苦難行苦行尚無怯畏，何況小苦。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, though there exist boundless worlds throughout the ten directions entirely free of suffering, choose instead to be born into worlds where suffering exists — worlds where suffering is constantly to be found, never absent.

items.title: Fearlessness Before Suffering Closes the Four Causes — Eight Kinds of Hardship, Willingly Faced

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩性自勇健，堪忍有力，當知是名第一因緣。又諸菩薩性自聰敏，能正思惟，具思擇力，當知是名第二因緣。又諸菩薩能於無上正等菩提成就上品清淨信解，當知是名第三因緣。又諸菩薩於諸眾生成就上品深心悲愍，當知是名第四因緣。
items.en: Bodhisattvas are by nature courageous, capable of enduring, and strong … by nature sharp and intelligent, able to reflect correctly, possessing the power of careful discernment … able to establish supreme, pure confidence and conviction in unsurpassed, perfect awakening … and able to establish supreme, profound compassion for beings — this last is the fourth condition for fearlessness.

items.title: Section: Four Powers Behind the Resolve — and Why Some Vows Hold Firm While Others Waver

items.zh: 云何四力？一者、自力，二者、他力，三者、因力，四者、加行力。謂諸菩薩由自功力，能於無上正等菩提深生愛樂，是名第一初發心力。又諸菩薩由他功力，能於無上正等菩提深生愛樂，是名第二初發心力。又諸菩薩宿習大乘相應善法，今暫得見諸佛菩薩，或暫得聞稱揚讚美，即能速疾發菩提心，況覩神力、聞其正法，是名第三初發心力。又諸菩薩於現法中，親近善士，聽聞正法，諦思惟等，長時修習種種善法，由此加行發菩提心，是名第四初發心力。
items.en: What are the four powers? First, one's own power; second, another's power; third, the power of past cause; fourth, the power of present effort … through one's own power, deep affection for unsurpassed awakening arises — this is the first … through another's power, this same affection arises — this is the second … through wholesome practices habituated towards the great vehicle in past lives, merely glimpsing the buddhas and bodhisattvas, or hearing them praised, is enough to swiftly raise the resolve — this is the third … through drawing near a genuine teacher in this very life, hearing the true teaching, reflecting on it carefully, and sustaining long practice of wholesome qualities, the resolve is raised through this very effort — this is the fourth.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩依上總別四緣、四因，或由自力、或由因力、或總二力而發心者，當知此心堅固無動。或由他力、或加行力、或總二力而發心者，當知此心不堅不固，亦非無動。
items.en: If bodhisattvas raise the resolve based on the conditions and causes described above, through their own power, or the power of past cause, or both together, one should know that resolve is firm and unshakeable … but if raised through another's power, or the power of present effort, or both together, one should know that resolve is neither firm nor stable, and not, in fact, unshakeable.

blocks.text: Why a degenerate age itself is a reason to make the vow, and the causes and powers that make the resolve firm.

Beings are disturbed by "much delusion, shamelessness, stinginess and envy, grief, unwieldiness of body and mind, affliction, wrongdoing, heedlessness, laziness, lack of faith". Master Cháng Bǎi on laziness: "attached to sleep, delighting in lying down." Seeing this: "Even those able to raise the lesser resolve of a hearer are hard to find; how much more the great resolve. I myself should raise it."
Complete lineage; being embraced by a true spiritual friend; compassion; and fearlessness before the long suffering of saṃsāra.

"Neither dull nor slow, but intelligent and discerning, never falling into wrong views"; never urging one to be heedless or to abandon "superior confidence, aspiration, training, diligence, or skilful means".
"Though there exist boundless worlds free of suffering, bodhisattvas choose to be born where suffering exists." "Courageous, enduring, strong": "even the hardest practices bring no fear."

One's own power ("deep affection for awakening"); another's power (encouraged by others); the power of past cause; and the power of present effort. A resolve raised by one's own power or past cause "is firm and unshakeable"; by another's power or present effort alone, it may waver.

quiz.q: "Much shamelessness (無慚愧)." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 慚 and 愧?
options: no sense of shame towards oneself, no embarrassment towards others
quiz.why: "Much delusion, much shamelessness, much stinginess and envy." Master Cháng Bǎi: not feeling ashamed with respect to oneself, not feeling embarrassed with respect to others — that's shamelessness.

quiz.q: "I should raise the resolve, so beings of this degenerate world follow my example." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: leading the beings of this five-turbidity age to follow me — thus raising the vow
quiz.why: "I myself should raise the great resolve for awakening, so that the boundless beings of this degenerate world may follow my example and likewise raise the aspiration for awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: to lead boundless beings of the five-turbidity world to follow me — thus one raises the vow for unsurpassed awakening.

quiz.q: The good friend's first mark: "never falling into wrong views." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: innate and cultivated wisdom across the five sciences — neither superimposing nor denying
quiz.why: "A bodhisattva's genuine spiritual friend is by nature neither dull nor slow, but intelligent and discerning, never falling into wrong views." Master Cháng Bǎi: having innate and cultivated wisdom, wise in all five sciences, not falling into wrong views — neither superimposing nor denying.

quiz.q: "Though painless worlds exist, choosing to be born where suffering exists." Why, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: insisting on rebirth in a suffering world — that's compassion
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, though there exist boundless worlds throughout the ten directions entirely free of suffering, choose instead to be born into worlds where suffering exists." Venerable Miào Jìng: he insists on being born into a world with suffering — that's because of compassion.

quiz.q: Fearlessness's first condition: "by nature courageous, enduring, strong." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: endurance and no fear of suffering come from past cultivation — so one can do the hard thing
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas are by nature courageous, capable of enduring, and strong." Master Cháng Bǎi: having endurance and strength, not fearing suffering — this comes from past cultivation, so the hard is doable.

quiz.q: Among the four powers, what is "the power of past cause," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
quiz.why: "What are the four powers? First, one's own power; second, another's power; third, the power of past cause; fourth, the power of present effort." Master Cháng Bǎi: third, the power of cause — power cultivated in past lives.

quiz.q: Own-power and past-cause resolve is "firm and unshakeable"; another's power and effort "neither firm nor stable." The note says the latter can mature. What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: 堅 is unbreakable, 固 deep-rooted; Miào Jìng: resolve moved by outer conditions is unreliable — it may retreat
quiz.why: "One should know that resolve is firm and unshakeable … but if raised through another's power, or the power of present effort, or both together, one should know that resolve is neither firm nor stable." Master Cháng Bǎi: 堅 is sturdy, unbreakable; 固 is deep-rooted, not to be tilted or uprooted. Venerable Miào Jìng: resolve raised because one was moved by outer conditions — that's unreliable! Sometimes it retreats. The note's softening isn't in the lectures.
